decisions_for_user.question: C: where does the unaccepted-evidence refusal live?
decisions_for_user.pre_authorised_default: In requirement_gate, as a sibling of GateRefusal.unmergeable and on the same rationale - `_check_mergeable`'s docstring already draws exactly this line ('rigor is a claim about how well the work must be proven; this is a claim about whether it can go where approval puts it') and GateRefusal already separates 'this cannot go in' from 'this is unproven'. It MUST be rigor-independent for the same reason _check_mergeable is. Cost if wrong: a refusal in the wrong module, cheap to move while nothing depends on its location.
decisions_for_user.raise_it_if: placing it there forces requirement_gate to import something that creates a cycle, or the refusal needs to fire somewhere apply_transition does not reach.

decisions_for_user.question: C: what exactly counts as 'evidence sits unaccepted'?
decisions_for_user.pre_authorised_default: Evidence rows for this task in review_state 'awaiting'. REJECTED evidence is NOT this case - it has been judged, and refusing on it would wedge a task whose author must now record better evidence. Name every awaiting row in the refusal, not just the count. Cost if wrong: an over- or under-broad refusal, found immediately by DRIVE-1.
decisions_for_user.raise_it_if: the honest predicate needs to distinguish evidence recorded against a requirement this task is not linked to.

decisions_for_user.question: C: a task with SOME accepted evidence naming a commit AND some still awaiting - refuse, or allow?
decisions_for_user.pre_authorised_default: ALLOW. The goal is that approval always merges something when there is something to merge; if accepted evidence already names a commit, integration will merge it and approval keeps its meaning. Refusing here would block work that is genuinely ready because a second piece of evidence is still in review. Record the awaiting rows as an advisory on the transition rather than a refusal. Cost if wrong: a task merges the older of two commits, visible in the integration record and correctable by a retry after acceptance.
decisions_for_user.raise_it_if: round 2 finds that the awaiting evidence routinely names a NEWER commit than the accepted one, which would make allowing it merge stale work.

decisions_for_user.question: D: how does a loop declare whether its work needs evidence, and what is the default?
decisions_for_user.pre_authorised_default: A column on Loop plus a create_loop parameter, defaulting to NOT requiring evidence. Rationale for that default: a loop today can never merge anything at all, so defaulting to evidence-free is what makes the feature work and regresses nothing - no existing loop is landing work that could break. Name it for what it means to the operator, not for the mechanism. Cost if wrong: a default that surprises someone whose loop starts merging; bounded because loop tasks are per-task-isolated branches.
decisions_for_user.raise_it_if: round 2 or 3 finds an existing loop path that DOES merge today, which would make this a behaviour change rather than a new capability.

decisions_for_user.question: D: when a loop needs no evidence, what commit is merged?
decisions_for_user.pre_authorised_default: The task's own branch, agentweave/task/<task_id>, because `work-is-isolated-per-task` guarantees it carries that task's work and nothing else - which is precisely the property F58 was about. VERIFY that guarantee holds for LOOP tasks specifically before relying on it; that change was written about flows. Do NOT merge an agent branch (agentweave/<agent>) - that is F58 exactly, and it ships every task the agent ever touched. Cost if wrong: the F58 class of defect, which is severity A, so verify rather than assume.
decisions_for_user.raise_it_if: loop tasks turn out not to get per-task worktrees, in which case there is no safe branch to merge and this needs the operator.

decisions_for_user.question: The drives will find new defects. Which get fixed unattended and which are merely filed?
decisions_for_user.pre_authorised_default: FIX what is small, self-contained and unambiguous - a wrong status code, a missing field, a message naming the wrong thing - each with a reproduction first and its own commit. FILE anything that needs a design decision, changes a lifecycle, touches a shipped requirement, or has more than one defensible answer. When in doubt, file it: a filed finding costs the operator two minutes to read, a wrong fix costs a spec loop to undo.
decisions_for_user.raise_it_if: a drive finds something severity A that blocks the rest of the run.

FOUND IN ITERATION 12 (D-R2), filed as F158 and NOT fixed: a task branch is cut at DISPATCH (`pending -> assigned`) and prerequisites are merged ONLY at branch creation (`worktrees.py:447-449`, `:481-487`), while `dependency_gate` fires one edge later on `-> in_progress`. `candidate_is_startable` closes this on the scheduler's path; `agent_trigger` consults no dependency gate AT ALL (grepped: no call site). So an operator triggering an agent on a task whose prerequisite is unapproved cuts its branch permanently without that work, and `POST /tasks/{id}/dependencies` can add an edge after a branch exists. Pre-existing on the evidence route; worse on the evidence-free route, whose only route home is a best-effort merge. The candidate repair is D-R3's standing decision.

FOUND IN ITERATION 12 (D-R2), recorded in the proposal's Impact and NOT closed: `TaskCreate.loop_id` is caller-supplied and agent-reachable (`tasks.py:771`, `schemas/tasks.py:63`, `mcp_server.py` `create_task`) and `TaskUpdate.loop_id` is write-once rather than immutable (`schemas/tasks.py:146-151`). So a task can be attached to an evidence-free loop after it exists, changing what approval writes into the operator's main branch. Approval stays gated and conflict-tested, so this widens what can be OFFERED, not what lands unasked. Narrowing `loop_id` is a change of its own.

FOUND IN ITERATION 11 (D-R1), filed as F157 and NOT fixed: `POST /jobs` accepts a loop field on a job that is not becoming a loop and silently drops it (`create_job` reads `spec_document_id` only inside `if _loop_opts_in(...)`), while `PATCH /jobs/{id}` refuses the same field naming the remedy (`jobs.py:856-876`). `agent-loops`' scenario is worded 'WHEN an UPDATE supplies a loop field', so the create path is outside the requirement rather than in breach of it. Change D deliberately does not inherit the precedent for its own field (design D4) because a dropped `spec_document_id` shows as a loop that never fills, while a dropped evidence declaration is invisible until an approval writes to the main branch.

FOUND IN ITERATION 10 (DRIVE-1), filed as F154 and NOT fixed: a review turn that ends without a verdict leaves the task `under_review` with its reviewer named, and every later firing reports it as DECISION_IN_FLIGHT -- 409 'Every task on this loop's queue is already being worked. Nothing was started, and nothing is wrong' -- with both agents idle and no run live. `held = tasks_held_by_a_running_turn(...)` is already computed before the walk and used by the ordinary-work arm to draw exactly this distinction; the WITH_REVIEWER branch never consults it. Same shape as F142, one door over, and it breaches the same requirement B was fixed against.

FOUND IN ITERATION 10 (DRIVE-1), filed as F155 and NOT fixed: the unmergeable refusal names a remedy that cannot work -- resolving on the branch makes a commit no evidence names, so `_check_mergeable`'s answer cannot change. What clears it is recording FRESH evidence naming the merged commit, which nothing says. Only reachable when a SECOND task has already landed on the main branch and touched the same paths, which is why three spec rounds and 3,555 unit tests did not have it. A product instruction that invited `git reset --hard` on a branch holding the only copy of an agent's work.

FOUND IN ITERATION 9 (C-IMPL), fixed in place and worth carrying as a lesson about the rounds: `tasks.md` 7.2 named `hub/tests/test_spec_evidence.py`, which does not exist -- written from memory in round 1 and copied through rounds 2 and 3 without being checked, because no round runs a command. Three independent re-derivations of the ARGUMENT cannot catch a file that is not there. D-R1 and D-R2 both applied the fix literally: every cited file was opened or grepped, and D-R2 corrected one line citation that way.

FOUND IN ITERATION 9 (C-IMPL), filed not fixed: task 6.2 as written ('the agent plane sees the refusal') asserted `detail["code"]` on a task still in `pending`, so the agent PATCH was refused by the LEGALITY check -- a plain-string detail -- long before the gate ran. A test asserting only '409' would have passed on entirely the wrong refusal and claimed the channel worked. Asserting a status code without asserting WHICH refusal is how a channel test passes without testing the channel.

FOUND IN ITERATION 6 (C-R1), filed not fixed and written into that change as tasks.md 8.3: `TaskResponse.approval_report` -- the only channel the product has for a report made at the moment of approval -- has NO UI consumer. Grepping `hub/ui/src` for it returns nothing. DRIVE-1 confirmed the grep and did not reach a mixed case, so 8.3 stays open. Note also that `approval_report` carries only `reported_advisories`, never an integration outcome, so an agent approving a task never learns whether its work merged.

FOUND IN ITERATION 5 (B-IMPL), FILED NOT FIXED, and queued as decisions_for_user D18: `record_evidence` takes `task_id` as a free parameter and does not require the calling run to be bound to it, so an agent can work a task on an UNBOUND run, record evidence naming its commit, and appear in NONE of the exclusion's three terms while `RequirementEvidence.actor` names it -- and the review arm requires that very row to exist before it resolves a reviewer at all.

FOUND IN ITERATION 5 (B-IMPL), FIXED, and worth carrying as a lesson about the rounds themselves: `task-lifecycle-governance`'s scenario was keyed on nothing but the absence of a completion, which implemented literally reports a REAL hand-dispatched review in progress as one nobody is doing. Every round checked the wedge predicate against being given the WIDER set -- three times -- and none checked the narrower direction.
